rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal clause is moved before its verb to foreground the moment, which answers the question about when resurrection comes.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم على عامله للاهتمام بالظرف لأنه المقصود من سياق مجاوبة قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text leaves the arrival of Resurrection unstated, since the question about escape and the final return already imply that its terrors have come.
rows.anchor: وطوي التصريح بأن ذلك حلول يوم القيامة اكتفاء بذكر ما يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated ‘that day’ stresses the day they denied and states that the three cosmic signs occur together; its tanwin stands for an omitted clause.
rows.anchor: فتنوين ( إذ ) تنوين عوض عن الجملة المحذوفة التي دلت عليها الجملة التي أضيف إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person asking where to flee is the disbeliever already mentioned in the surah, and the question expresses a wish for a place of escape.
rows.anchor: و { الإنسان } : هو المتحدث عنه من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mafar is a verbal noun meaning flight, while the interrogative is a wish for refuge that cannot be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في التمني ، أي ليت لي فرارا في مكان نجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes the hope of escape; a wazar is a refuge such as mountains or fortresses where one seeks protection.
rows.anchor: ردع وإبطال لما تضمنه { أين المفر } من الطمع في أن يجد للفرار سبيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause denying any refuge may be God's answer, requiring a pause after ‘where to flee,’ or the person's own despairing answer, allowing the clauses to run together.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون { كلا لا وزر } كلاما مستأنفا من جانب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative reading in which the person answers himself, he looks around and sees only Fire, as a hadith reports.
rows.anchor: وذلك بأن نظر في جهاته فلم يجد إلا النار كما ورد في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘To your Lord is the final resort’ is God's address to the Prophet in worldly time, inserted to remind him of God's sovereignty over that Day.
rows.anchor: فهو كلام من جانب الله تعالى خاطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Prophet's Lord hints that He will support him by requiting those who rejected his message.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى أنه ناصره يومئذ بالانتقام من الذين لم يقبلوا دعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mustaqarr is an intensified place-or-state noun derived from istaqarra, ‘to settle.’
rows.anchor: مصدر ميمي من استقر ، إذا قر في المكان ولم ينتقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting ‘to your Lord’ makes the destination exclusive: no other refuge exists, as in the declaration that all return is to God.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المجرور لإفادة الحصر ، أي إلى ربك لا إلى ملجأ آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announcement that a person will be told his deeds is an explanatory resumption prompted by the final return, or an inclusive substitute for it.
rows.anchor: مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا أثاره قوله : { إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر } ، أو بدل اشتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although everyone is informed of deeds, ‘the human’ here means the disbeliever addressed by the context; similar wording in different Qur'anic settings need not have one referent.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن يكون المراد ب { الإنسان } الكافر جريا على سياق الآيات السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being informed of what one did is a metonym for receiving its recompense: the deed is identified, exposing and rebuking its doer.
rows.anchor: وتنبئة الإنسان بما قدم وأخر كناية عن مجازاته على ما فعله : إن خيرا فخير وإن سوءا فسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What a person brought forward means what he did; what he left behind includes duties or prohibitions left unfulfilled, as in the Prophet's supplication for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ما فعله وب { ما أخر } : ما تركه مما أمر بفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage advances from the report of deeds to the disbeliever's awareness of them through bodily testimony and the opened record of actions.
rows.anchor: إضراب انتقالي ، وهو للترقي من مضمون { ينبأ الإنسان يومئذ بما قدم وأخر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical reading makes ‘insightful’ a predicate for the person: he sees and closely monitors himself, with ‘upon’ carrying the sense of watching.
rows.anchor: أولهما أن يكون { بصيرة } بمعنى مبصر شديد المراقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading makes ‘insightful’ a second predicate for the person's recording angel, who watches over him.
rows.anchor: أن يكون { بصيرة } مبتدأ ثانيا ، والمراد به قرين الإنسان من الحفظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘insight’ can mean a manifest proof, with an omitted noun such as ‘a clear proof’; the feminine form agrees with that noun.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون { بصيرة } صفة لموصوف محذوف ، تقديره : حجة بصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah was called ‘Hal ata ala al-insan’ in the Prophet's Companions' era; other names include al-Insan, al-Dahr, al-Amshaj, and al-Abrar, though the last is reported only by al-Tabrisi.
rows.anchor: فهذه خمسة أسماء لهذه السورة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari reports that the Prophet recited alif-lam-mim al-sajda and Hal ata al-insan in the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري في باب القراءة في الفجر من ( صحيحه ) عن أبي هريرة قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن أبي طلحة وقتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: These authorities hold that the surah is Meccan; Ibn Masud's codex arrangement also supports that classification.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس وابن أبي طلحة وقتادة ومقاتل : هي مكية

rows.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس وجابر بن زيد
rows.claim: This reported view classifies the surah as Medinan; Qatada is also reported to have held this view.
rows.anchor: وروى مجاهد عن ابن عباس : أنها مدنية ، وهو قول جابر بن زيد

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة والكلبي
rows.claim: They regard the surah as Medinan except for the closing passage beginning at verse 24, though they do not identify an earlier surah in which it was recited.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وعكرمة والكلبي : هي مدنية إلا قوله : { ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is more likely Meccan because its style and themes match Meccan revelation; reports about verse 8 prompted the Medinan classification but may be later applications mistaken for occasions of revelation.
rows.anchor: والأصح أنها مكية فإن أسلوبها ومعانيها جارية على سنن السور المكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence may be parsed as a circumstantial clause from ‘the human,’ with its resumptive pronoun omitted.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الجملة حالا من { الإنسان } ، وحذف العائد كحذفه في تقدير النعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ‘thing’ is an existent; ‘mentioned’ means specifically identified and named, not merely categorized, so the verse describes a person not yet existing as a distinct individual.
rows.anchor: والمذكور : المعين الذي هو بحيث يذكر ، أي يعبر عنه بخصوصه ويخبر عنه بالأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next statement answers the suspenseful rhetorical question: God brought humanity into being after nonexistence, first creating a reproductive drop.
rows.anchor: والتقرير يقتضي الإقرار بذلك لا محالة لأنه معلوم بالضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic particle treats idolaters as deniers of God's creation because they worship objects that did not create them.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الكلام بحرف ( إن ) لتنزيل المشركين منزلة من ينكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The human’ denotes the whole human kind, and the account of reproductive creation embeds evidence of divine knowledge, power, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب { الإنسان } مثل ما أريد به في قوله : { هل أتى على الإنسان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amshaj derives from mixing: it describes a mixed drop, as creation of pairs from earthly growth and other sources illustrates.
rows.anchor: مشتق من المشج وهو الخلط ، أي نطفة مخلوطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farra, Ibn al-Sikkit, and al-Mubarrad take amshaj as a plural form, with possible singular patterns meaning ‘mixed.’
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك حملها الفراء وابن السكيت والمبرد ، فهي إما جمع مشج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering the Lord's name includes proclaiming the message, obligatory and voluntary worship, and exhorting people through fear of punishment and hope for reward.
rows.anchor: وذكر اسم الرب يشمل تبليغ الدعوة ويشمل عبادة الله في الصلوات المفروضة والنوافل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Morning and evening’ covers the day's set prayer times as well as voluntary prayer, supplication, and seeking forgiveness; the terms mean early day and late day.
rows.anchor: يشمل أوقات النهار كلها المحدود منها كأوقات الصلوات وغير المحدود كأوقات النوافل ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to prostrate at night refers specifically to night prayer, obligatory or voluntary, when the Prophet is free from public preaching.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الليل وقت تفرغ من بث الدعوة كما تقدم في قوله : { قم الليل إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because glorification is coordinated with night prostration, it refers here to voluntary devotion; tasbih also includes verbal praise, good speech, and reflection on God's attributes.
rows.anchor: فتعين أن التسبيح التنفل . والتسبيح : التنزيه بالقول وبالاعتقاد

rows.speaker: عبد الملك بن حبيب
rows.claim: He interprets ‘glorify Him’ here as voluntary night prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الملك بن حبيب : و { سبحه } هنا صلاة التطوع في الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘A long night’ restricts the command to glorify: spend most of the night in worship, as in the instruction to stand except for a little.
rows.anchor: فتعين أن وصف الطول تقييد للأمر بالتسبيح ، أي سبحه أكثر الليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
rows.claim: They read morning and evening as the five prescribed prayers and their times, taking ‘evening’ to include noon; glorification then points to night prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وابن زيد : أن هاتين الآيتين إشارة إلى الصلوات الخمس وأوقاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These instructions echo commands to glorify God, prostrate, remember Him, and persevere despite opponents' words.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية جاءت على وفق قوله تعالى : { ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has five attested names: al-Naba, Amma yatasa'alun, Amma, al-Tasa'ul, and al-Mu'asirat; al-Itqan lists four. It is Meccan and was placed after al-Ma'arij and before al-Nazi'at in Jabir ibn Zayd's revelation order.
rows.anchor: فهذه خمسة أسماء . واقتصر في ( الإتقان ) على أربعة أسماء : عم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He reports that Quraysh discussed the newly revealed Quran among themselves, some affirming it and others denying it, prompting the opening question.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس : ( كانت قريش تجلس لما نزل القرآن فتتحدث فيما بينها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says that when the Prophet was sent, people began asking one another about the great announcement, and the opening verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن لما بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جعلوا يتساءلون بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medinan, Syrian, and Basran counters count forty verses; Meccan and Kufan counters count forty-one.
rows.anchor: وعد آيها أصحاب العدد من أهل المدينة والشام والبصرة أربعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah rebukes mockery of the Quran and resurrection, proves resurrection through creation and humanity's first creation, warns of punishment, and contrasts believers' reward.
rows.anchor: اشتملت هذه السورة على وصف خوض المشركين في شأن القرآن وما جاء به مما يخالف معتقداتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Bring forth’ rather than ‘grow’ portrays resurrection from the earth as the passage's main point; in Qaf, where favor is foregrounded, growth comes first and resurrection follows as an inference.
rows.anchor: وجيء بفعل { لنخرج } دون نحو : لننبت ، لأن المقصود الإيماء إلى تصوير كيفية بعث الناس من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grain is a collective for edible seeds, including wheat, barley, millet, corn, rice, and pulses.
rows.anchor: والحب : اسم جمع حبة وهي البرزة . والمراد بالحب هنا : الحب المقتات للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabat is originally a verbal noun, then a conventional noun for useful vegetation whose seeds are not eaten, such as straw, clover, and grass.
rows.anchor: والنبات أصله اسم مصدر نبت الزرع ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Gardens’ stands for their trees; the word evokes generous shade, fruit, water, and beauty, while ‘dense’ adds beauty even though farmers may prefer spacing for yield.
rows.anchor: ووجه إيثار لفظ { جنات } أن فيه إيماء إلى إتمام المنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announcement of the Day of Decision explains the opening question about the great news; placing it after crops produced by rain makes their emergence an image for resurrection.
rows.anchor: هذا بيان لما أجمله قوله : { عن النبإ العظيم الذي هم فيه مختلفون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Decision is the day of resurrection and recompense; the confirmed statement counters the disbelievers' denial.
rows.anchor: وأكد الكلام بحرف التأكيد لأن فيه إبطالا لإنكار المشركين وتكذيبهم بيوم الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasl means separating what is mixed, then came to mean distinguishing ambiguous matters and adjudicating; recompense separates people from one another.
rows.anchor: والفصل : التمييز بين الأشياء المختلطة ، وشاع إطلاقه على التمييز بين المعاني المتشابهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it the Day of Decision confirms both resurrection and recompense and God's judgment among people over their disputes and mutual wrongs.
rows.anchor: وأوثر التعبير عنه بيوم الفصل لإثبات شيئين : أحدهما : أنه بين ثبوت ما جحدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ‘was’ makes the appointed time established in God's wisdom, so their demand cannot bring it forward.
rows.anchor: وإقحام فعل { كان } لإفادة أن توقيته متأصل في علم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miqat derives from time and means a fixed time; here the context supplies resurrection and recompense as what has its appointed time.
rows.anchor: والميقات : مفعال مشتق من الوقت ، والوقت : الزمان المحدد في عمل ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative ‘provision’ stands in place of an omitted verb: ‘We provided you with provision.’
rows.anchor: وانتصب { متاعا } على النيابة عن الفعل . والتقدير : متعناكم متاعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lams in ‘for you and your livestock’ reinforce the verbal noun; earth and mountains provide use, shelter from enemies, and safe pasture.
rows.anchor: ولام { لكم ولأنعامكم } لام التقوية لأن المصدر فرع في العمل عن الفعل ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning provision inside the proof embeds gratitude, inviting people to worship their benefactor alone; the wording also uses a blend-then-division figure.
rows.anchor: وهذا إدماج الامتنان في الاستدلال لإثارة شكرهم حق النعمة بأن يعبدوا المنعم وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning and glad tidings follow the proof of resurrection because judgment follows resurrection; the wise prepare for lasting reward rather than transient pleasure.
rows.anchor: فإن إثبات البعث يقتضي الجزاء إذ هو حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning moves from the resurrection's first convulsion to the blast and then the Great Calamity, a term encompassing all horrors until each group reaches its abode.
rows.anchor: ثم بالزجرة ، وأخيرا بالطامة الكبرى لما في هذين الوصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder of judgment follows the creation and provision of the earth because those worldly comforts end when resurrection and judgment arrive.
rows.anchor: ومن تمام المناسبة للتذكير بيوم الجزاء وقوعه عقب التذكير بخلق الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Great Calamity branches from the single blast and is itself that blast.
rows.anchor: على قوله : { فإنما هي زجرة واحدة فإذا هم بالساهرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaders prefer worldly life because, despite recognizing the Messenger's truth, they resent following another and losing their authority.
rows.anchor: فإن سادتهم ومسيريهم يعلمون أن ما يدعوهم إليه الرسول هو الحق ولكنهم يكرهون متابعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blame concerns choosing worldly life over the afterlife; worldly benefits that do not cost one the afterlife are not blameworthy, as the counsel to Qarun shows.
rows.anchor: فأما الأخذ بحظوظ الحياة الدنيا التي لا يفيت الأخذ بها حظوظ الآخرة فذلك غير مذموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses are parallel: fearing the Lord counters transgression, while restraining the self from desire counters preferring worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { من خاف مقام ربه } مقابل قوله : { من طغى } لأن الخوف ضد الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restraining one's self personifies it as another who urges sin; this rhetorical self-separation is illustrated by Urwa ibn Udhayna's verse about heart and conscience.
rows.anchor: وهذا يشبه ما يسمى بالتجريد ، يقولون : قالت له نفسه كذا فعصاها

rows.speaker: عروة بن أذينة
rows.claim: His verse illustrates the inner dialogue by which the heart appeals to conscience to restrain the self's impulses.
rows.anchor: ومن أحسن ما قيل في ذلك قول عروة بن أذينة : وإذا وجدت لها وساوس سلوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawa means what the soul desires, especially appetites or anger contrary to truth and complete benefit; since such desire is unguided, ‘without guidance’ in 28:50 is emphatic.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب { الهوى } ما تهواه النفس فهو مصدر بمعنى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic definite article in al-hawa denotes the class of desire.
rows.anchor: وتعريف { الهوى } تعريف الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite articles in the two ‘abode’ phrases refer back to the abode of each group; Basran and Kufan grammarians differ over whether the article replaces an omitted possessive or modifies an implied possessive construction.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { المأوى } الأول والثاني تعريف العهد ، أي مأوى من طغى ، ومأوى من خاف مقام ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma'wa is a place noun from ‘return’; it means a person's settled dwelling, where one returns after attending to other affairs.
rows.anchor: والمأوى : اسم مكان من أوى ، إذا رجع ، فالمراد به : المقر والمسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The station of his Lord’ figuratively conveys divine majesty and awe, naming the place of standing for what is associated with it.
rows.anchor: و { مقام ربه } مجاز عن الجلال والمهابة وأصل المقام مكان القيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired descriptions of remembering and the Garden use a collect-then-divide rhetorical structure; ‘the self’ has the same generic definite sense as ‘the abode.’
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى } إلى قوله : { فإن الجنة هي المأوى } محسن الجمع مع التقسيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the people of Fire and Garden with relative clauses hints that each clause is the cause of its group deserving that abode.
rows.anchor: وفي تعريف ( أصحاب الجحيم ) و ( أصحاب الجنة ) بطريق الموصول إيماء إلى أن الصلتين علتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about the Hour begins an explanatory resumption prompted by the disbelievers' repeated, mocking questions about its timing and their demand that it be hastened.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني منشؤه أن المشركين كانوا يسألون عن وقت حلول الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They imagine the delay disproves the Hour, reasoning that an angry God would immediately retaliate like an impetuous human; the Quran rejects this human analogy.
rows.anchor: وكان سؤالهم استهزاء واستخفافا لأنهم عقدوا قلوبهم على استحالة وقوع الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proving resurrection and describing its punishment, the passage answers the question about when the Great Calamity will arrive.
rows.anchor: لما قضي حق الاستدلال على إمكان البعث بإقامة الدليل وضرب الأمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners are the disbelievers who earlier asked whether they would be restored to their former state.
rows.anchor: فضمير ( يسألون ) عائد إلى المشركين أصحاب القلوب الواجفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb presents their question as recurring and repeated.
rows.anchor: وحكي فعل السؤال بصيغة المضارع للدلالة على تجدد هذا السؤال وتكرره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Hour ‘the Hour’ rather than repeating ‘the Great Calamity’ gives the sentence independent force and varies the naming.
rows.anchor: والساعة : هي الطامة فذكر الساعة إظهار في مقام الإضمار لقصد استقلال الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyan asks for a specific time; the question implies that the event is remote or even impossible, while marsa is a ship's mooring metaphor for the Hour's arrival.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام مستعمل في الاستبعاد كناية وهو أيضا كناية عن الاستحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply redirects their demand for a date toward what matters: the Prophet's task is to warn those who fear the Hour, a ‘wise style’ like the Prophet asking a questioner what he had prepared.
rows.anchor: فهذا الجواب من تخريج الكلام على خلاف مقتضى الظاهر ، وهو من تلقي السائل بغير ما يتطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in an authentic collection says that when a man asked the Prophet about the Hour, he asked what the man had prepared for it.
rows.anchor: ونظيره ما روي في الصحيح أن رجلا سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الساعة فقال له : ( ماذا أعددت لها ؟ )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although addressed to the Prophet, the response is meant for the disbelievers to hear, and its separation from the question marks it as an answer.
rows.anchor: والخطاب وإن كان موجها إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فالمقصود بلوغه إلى مسامع المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative ‘what’ expresses astonishment at and rebuke of their question.
rows.anchor: و ( ما ) في قوله : { فيم } اسم استفهام بمعنى : أي شيء ؟ مستعملة في التعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ‘in’ figuratively depicts them as surrounding the Prophet with questions about the Hour, as if he were occupied with knowledge of its date.
rows.anchor: فدل على ذلك بحرف الظرفية على طريقة الاستعارة في الحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif of ma is dropped after the preposition, as in the opening of al-Naba; fima is the fronted predicate and anta its subject.
rows.anchor: وحذف ألف ( ما ) لوقوعها بعد حرف الجر مثل { عم يتساءلون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min may explain the interrogative's ambiguity as ‘something that is its reminder,’ or describe a relation: the Prophet has no involvement with determining the Hour's time.
rows.anchor: و { من } : إما مبينة للإبهام الذي في ( ما ) الاستفهامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting fima emphasizes that the Prophet's involvement in the Hour's remembrance is what the question rebukes.
rows.anchor: وتقديم { فيم } على المبتدأ للاهتمام به ليفيد أن مضمون الخبر هو مناط الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikra is a verbal noun meaning spoken remembrance in this context.
rows.anchor: والذكرى : اسم مصدر الذكر ، والمراد به هنا الذكر اللساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘To your Lord is its end’ explains why the Prophet is not involved: knowledge of the Hour's end belongs exclusively to God.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إلى ربك منتهاها } في موقع العلة للإنكار الذي اقتضاه قوله : { فيم أنت من ذكراها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muntaha began as the place where a journey ends, then came to mean destiny and, by extension, knowledge; an omitted noun is ‘knowledge of its time.’
rows.anchor: ثم توسع فيه فأطلق على العلم ، أي لا يعلمها إلا الله ، فقوله : { منتهاها } هو في المعنى على حذف مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, its end may mean the point at which news of the Hour reaches someone.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { منتهاها } بمعنى بلوغ خبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's role is to warn of the Hour's sudden arrival, not announce its date; disbelievers wrongly treat silence about timing as proof against the Hour and assume he knows the unseen.
rows.anchor: فأجيب بأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حظه التحذير من بغتتها ، وليس حظه الإعلام بتعيين وقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innama restricts the Prophet to the function of warning, countering their assumption that he has access to the unseen.
rows.anchor: وأفادت { إنما } قصر المخاطب على صفة الإنذار ، أي تخصيصه بحال الإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use an annexed form of mundhir; Abu Ja'far reads it with nunation, making ‘those who fear it’ its object.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { منذر من يخشاها } قرأه الجمهور بإضافة { منذر } إلى { من يخشاها } . وقرأه أبو جعفر بتنوين { منذر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction implies ‘warner of it, so whoever fears it takes warning’: the Prophet addresses all, but only those who fear the Hour benefit, honoring believers and shaming unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وفي إضافة { منذر } إلى { من يخشاها } أو نصبه به إيجاز حذف تقديره : منذرها فينتذر من يخشاها ، وقرينة ذلك حالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are still called to faith and piety despite God's foreknowledge, since that knowledge is hidden from people and an individual's end appears only after death; the theologians call this muwafat.
rows.anchor: فمن مات منهم في ذلك فهو ممن لم يتق الله لأن ما في علم الله لا يبلغ الناس إلى علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply addresses the apparent request for timing and their use of delay to deny the Hour: it will occur, and the waiting will seem no longer than part of a day.
rows.anchor: فأجيبوا على طريقة الأسلوب الحكيم ، أي إن طال تأخر حصولها فإنها واقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening with two verbs whose pronouns lack an antecedent creates suspense; later references to the blind man and the rich man clarify the people and event.
rows.anchor: افتتاح هذه السورة بفعلين متحملين لضمير لا معاد له في الكلام تشويق لما سيورد بعدهما

rows.speaker: مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه
rows.claim: In a mursal report, Ibn Umm Maktum came asking to be brought near while the Prophet addressed a Meccan notable; the opening was revealed when the Prophet turned toward the notable. Al-Tirmidhi transmits a similar report from Urwa via Aisha and grades it hasan gharib.
rows.anchor: وهو ما رواه مالك في ( الموطأ ) مرسلا عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه أنه قال : أنزلت { عبس وتولى } في ابن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Provision for you’ is a circumstantial phrase applying to all the preceding items; ‘for your livestock’ is coordinated with ‘for you.’
rows.anchor: وقوله : { متاعا لكم } حال من المذكورات يعود إلى جميعها على قاعدة ورود الحال بعد مفردات متعاطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mata is a benefit that lasts for a time and ends; the listener matches each listed provision with its proper recipient, and the phrase embeds admonition and grace in the proof.
rows.anchor: والمتاع : ما ينتفع به زمنا ثم ينقطع ، وفيه لف ونشر مشوش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning of judgment follows the rebuke and the proof from creation and food, fitting the preceding reminders of provision, as in the Great Calamity passage in al-Nazi'at.
rows.anchor: الفاء للتفريع على اللوم والتوبيخ في قوله : { قتل الإنسان ما أكفره }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min can mark the cause of fleeing, as in fleeing from a lion, or mean separation, like an; both readings fit the passage.
rows.anchor: وحرف ( من ) هنا يجوز أن يكون بمعنى التعليل الذي يعدى به فعل الفرار إلى سبب الفرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fleeing from one's closest relatives reveals the day's terror: people imagine flight from those undergoing punishment may save them, though they know they share their deeds.
rows.anchor: وكون أقرب الناس للإنسان يفر منهم يقتضي هول ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence climbs in closeness: brotherhood begins in childhood, parents are closer, the mother is named first for stronger attachment and rhyme, then spouse and children form the household.
rows.anchor: ورتبت أصناف القرابة في الآية حسب الصعود من الصنف إلى من هو أقوى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listing each relative instead of saying ‘nearest kin’ vividly brings the terror before the listener.
rows.anchor: وأطنب بتعداد هؤلاء الأقرباء دون أن يقال : يوم يفر المرء من أقرب قرابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ‘his companion’ implies a woman fleeing her companion by ellipsis; it signals intimacy better than ‘wife,’ since some marriages lack good companionship.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكرت بوصف الصاحبة الدال على القرب والملازمة دون وصف الزوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more plausible reading is a believer fleeing disbelieving relatives to avoid being held accountable for their persistence in unbelief.
rows.anchor: والأقرب أن هذا فرار المؤمن من قرابته المشركين خشية أن يؤاخذ بتبعتهم

rows.claim: ‘Provision for you’ is a circumstantial phrase applying to all the preceding items; ‘for your livestock’ is coordinated with ‘for you.’
rows.anchor: وقوله : { متاعا لكم } حال من المذكورات يعود إلى جميعها على قاعدة ورود الحال بعد مفردات متعاطفة

rows.claim: The wording ‘his companion’ implies a woman fleeing her companion by ellipsis; it signals intimacy better than ‘wife,’ since some marriages lack good companionship.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكرت بوصف الصاحبة الدال على القرب والملازمة دون وصف الزوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more plausible reading is a believer fleeing disbelieving relatives to avoid being held accountable for their persistence in unbelief.
rows.anchor: والأقرب أن هذا فرار المؤمن من قرابته المشركين خشية أن يؤاخذ بتبعتهم

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Their readings do not conflict with the written codex, since its spelling can reflect pausal forms and pauses often affect orthography.
rows.anchor: فلا يوهن رسم المصحف روايتهم لأن رسم المصحف جاء على مراعاة حال الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is parenthetical between the oath and its answer or proof, as in the Quran's oath in al-Waqi'a.
rows.anchor: جملة معترضة بين القسم وما بعده من جوابه أو دليل جوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hal is confirmatory here, reflecting its original force of establishing a fact like qad; the demonstrative refers to the objects sworn by.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام تقريري ، وكونه بحرف { هل } لأن أصل { هل } أن تدل على التحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite qasam magnifies the oath as sufficient and compelling for a rational listener; hijr means intellect because it restrains its possessor from wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وتنكير { قسم } للتعظيم أي قسم كافف ومقنع للمقسم له .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in ‘for one of reason’ gives the oath its purpose: a rational person should not stubbornly deny the oath-taker's truth.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله : { لذي حجر } لام التعليل ، أي قسم لأجل ذي عقل يمنعه من المكابرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of earlier nations is not the direct oath answer; it either evidences an implied threat of like punishment or prepares for the explicit answer that God watches the deniers.
rows.anchor: لا يصلح هذا أن يكون جوابا للقسم ولكنه : إما دليل الجواب إذ يدل على أن المقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about earlier nations reassures the Prophet and warns opponents by analogy; recalling precedents makes seemingly unlikely punishment feel near.
rows.anchor: فالاستفهام في قوله : { ألم تر } تقريري ، والمخاطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تثبيتا له

rows.speaker: طرفة
rows.claim: Tarafa's lines voice the pre-Islamic boast that wealth, noble children, and status reflect divine favor and rank.
rows.anchor: قال طرفة : فلو شاء ربي كنت قيس بن عاصم ولو شاء ربي كنت عمرو بن مرثد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh, Tamim, and others asked the Prophet to expel poor believers so they might follow him; they made the same request of Abu Talib, and verse 6:52 addressed this error.
rows.anchor: قالوا للنبيء أطردهم عنك فلعلك إن طردتهم أن نتبعك .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly status is no measure of merit or final recompense; earlier peoples held similar delusions and were punished, while judgment belongs to the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وأعلمهم أن أحوال الدنيا لا تتخذ أصلا في اعتبار الجزاء على العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators do not explain how the passage's argument connects to its context, apart from al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Atiyya.
rows.anchor: ولم يعرج أكثر المفسرين على بيان نظم الآية واتصالها بما قبلها عدا الزمخشري وابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insan is grammatically generic, but its customary scope here is the disbelieving Meccans who dominate the discourse, as in several Meccan passages.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس وتعريفه تعريف الجنس فيستغرق أفراد الجنس ولكنه استغراق عرفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated indefinite ‘row upon row’ is not redundant confirmation; it adds arrangement or classification, such as separate rows for each class of angels. Al-Radi illustrates the pattern with repeated nouns.
rows.anchor: و { صفا } الثاني لم يختلف المفسرون في أنه من التكرير المراد به الترتيب والتصنيف ، أي صفا بعد صف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported view says angels of each heaven form a separate row around the earth.
rows.anchor: قيل : ملائكة كل سماء يكونون صفا حول الأرض على حدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ‘coming’ can be a rational attribution meaning His decree comes, or a metaphor for the beginning of reckoning as arrival.
rows.anchor: وإسناد المجيء إلى الله إما مجاز عقلي ، أي جاء قضاؤه ، وإما استعارة بتشبيه ابتداء حسابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' coming may be literal or mean their presence; the verb can therefore be used literally and figuratively, or in two figurative senses.
rows.anchor: وأما إسناده إلى الملك فإما حقيقة ، أو على معنى الحضور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malak is a generic noun with a definite article that denotes all angels; saff is both arranging objects in a line and the resulting row.
rows.anchor: و { الملك } : اسم جنس وتعريفه تعريف الجنس فيرادفه الاستغراق ، أي والملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing Hell means displaying and opening it, like the cited passages about its doors and the exposed Fire; an authentic report gives its supernatural dragging.
rows.anchor: واستعمال { وجيء يومئذ بجهنم } كاستعمال مجيء الملك ، أي أحضرت جهنم وفتحت أبوابها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود عن النبي
rows.claim: A report in Muslim says Hell is drawn by seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels; the author treats afterlife events as supernatural.
rows.anchor: وورد في حديث مسلم عن ابن مسعود يرفعه : ( أن لجهنم سبعين ألف زمام مع كل زمام سبعون ألف ملك يجرونها )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage mentions Hell because it warns those who ignored admonition; Paradise is also brought near, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: وإنما اقتصر على ذكر جهنم لأن المقصود في هذه السورة وعيد الذين لم يتذكروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first ‘that day’ attaches to ‘brought’; the second replaces the clause about the earth being crushed and is governed with it by ‘remember.’ Fronting stresses the time and builds suspense after a long interruption.
rows.anchor: و { يومئذ } الأول متعلق بفعل { جيء } . والتقدير : وجيء يوم تدك الأرض دكا دكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The human’ is the disbeliever already introduced in verse 15; it is repeated rather than pronominalized because the antecedent is distant.
rows.anchor: و { الإنسان } : هو الإنسان الكافر ، وهو الذي تقدم ذكره في قوله تعالى : { فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Where could remembrance benefit him?’ is an interposed rhetorical question denying that a reminder can now help him.
rows.anchor: و { أنى } اسم استفهام بمعنى : أين له الذكرى ، وهو استفهام مستعمل في الإنكار والنفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lament may be spoken aloud, as a circumstantial clause or inclusive substitute for remembering, or be an inward thought explaining the remembrance.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { يقول يا ليتني } الخ يجوز أن يكون قولا باللسان تحسرا وتندما فتكون الجملة حالا من { الإنسان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘I sent ahead’ is omitted for brevity and means good deeds.
rows.anchor: ومفعول { قدمت } محذوف للإيجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in ‘for my life’ may mean during the first life or for the purpose of attaining a complete life free from punishment, unlike the diminished existence of Hell.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله : { لحياتي } تحتمل معنى التوقيت ، أي قدمت عند أزمان حياتي
